ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law No. 80 of 2002 on Combating Money Laundering, as amended; Presidential and Ministerial Executive Regulations thereunder; Law No. 159 of 1981 on Joint Stock Companies, Partnerships Limited by Shares, and Limited Liability Companies, as amended, including provisions imposing beneficial ownership disclosure; regulations and circulars of the General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) and the Egyptian Anti-Money Laundering, Combating the Financing of Terrorism Commission.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the passport of each natural-person shareholder or ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) holding 25% or more of share capital or voting rights
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary / competent authority in the shareholder's country of origin or Egypt
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization (Arab Republic of Egypt is not a State Party to the Hague Apostille Convention; documents must be authenticated by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the origin country and subsequently legalized by the Egyptian Embassy or Consulate)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation and good standing of any corporate shareholder/UBO entity
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official companies registry in the jurisdiction of incorporation of the corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization via the Egyptian Embassy or Consulate after prior certification by the competent registry and origin-country Ministry of Foreign Affairs

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Duly executed Power of Attorney for the incorporation agent and/or local manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Public notary in the jurisdiction of execution or Egyptian public notary if executed in Egypt
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization if executed abroad; if executed in Egypt, notarization before an Egyptian public notary is sufficient

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Beneficial Ownership Declaration and structural organogram form
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: GAFI official registration form, signed by the incorporators and/or manager before an Egyptian public notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarization in Egypt and filing with GAFI; no apostille required when executed domestically

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory risk-based customer due diligence in accordance with Egyptian AML Law No. 80 of 2002, FATF Recommendations, OFAC and UN Security Council sanctions lists, EU consolidated sanctions lists, Central Bank of Egypt terrorist financing lists, and the Egyptian national terrorism lists issued by the Public Prosecutor. Politically Exposed Persons (PEPs) and their family members or close associates must be screened at the engagement stage and during any beneficial ownership change, with source-of-wealth documentation required for higher-risk profiles before company incorporation.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: GAFI Company Registry / Investor Registration e-Portal (General Authority for Investment and Free Zones), official website https://www.gafi.gov.eg
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: A proposed LLC name may be registered in Arabic; where an English or other Latin-script trade name is desired, the name must also be filed in its Arabic phonetic transliteration to permit matching against existing registered names and to comply with the Commercial Registry's Arabic record requirements. The name must not be identical or confusingly similar to any existing Egyptian company, trademark, or reserved name.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The applicant may apply for a one-time extension of the name reservation before the expiry of the initial 30-day period through the GAFI portal. If the name is rejected, the applicant may submit an administrative appeal to the GAFI Registration Committee within 30 days of the rejection notice, stating the grounds of objection and any revised name alternatives. GAFI will issue a decision within 30 business days. A further appeal may be filed with the competent Egyptian Economic Court against a final administrative refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not Permissible as the sole registered office for a designer blind box toy manufacturing LLC. The company must maintain a physical registered office in Egypt capable of receiving correspondence, preserving corporate books, and supervising operational records. A virtual office may be used only for auxiliary e-commerce marketing or administrative support, not as a substitute for the statutorily registered address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Estimated at approximately 40% to 50% during the first year of operations for a manufacturing and tax-registered LLC with physical production activity; GAFI, the Industrial Development Authority, the Tax Authority, and labour/safety regulators may conduct unannounced on-site inspections to verify commercial substance, headcount, equipment, and inventory.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Real estate lessor / registered office service provider / GAFI

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law No. 159 of 1981 (Companies Law of Egypt), as amended by Law No. 72 of 2017 (Investment Law) and Law No. 148 of 2019; LLC provisions under Articles 75-113; Executive Regulations of the Companies Law.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Companies Registration Department, in coordination with the Commercial Registry office
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association (Aqd wa Nitham Asasi) on the GAFI model LLC form, followed by issuance of the GAFI electronic incorporation certificate
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for a standard LLC; the Articles must state the capital, and cash contributions are paid into the LLC's bank account opened after GAFI issuance. There is no mandatory escrow account at incorporation, except where an IDA project license requires proof of funds or project financing.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: The initial subscriber hereby subscribes for and pays the entire issued share capital of the Company as recorded in the Articles of Association, and accepts all shares allocated to the founding shareholders. FURTHER RESOLVED: The registered office of the Company is fixed at [Address], [City], Egypt, and it shall be the official address for legal notices and statutory correspondence. FURTHER RESOLVED: [Full Name] is appointed Chief Manager and [Full Name] is appointed Secretary/Manager, each with authority, acting singly or jointly, to execute incorporation filings, open bank accounts, and apply for the IDA industrial license and EEAA environmental approvals. The board instructs officers to complete all registration procedures.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA), official portal https://www.eta.gov.eg/
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Foreign-owned LLCs must register with the Egyptian Tax Authority by submitting required documents including commercial registration certificate, ownership proof, and business plan via the ETA portal or in person at designated offices. Upon approval, a Tax Registration Number (TRN) is issued for VAT and income tax purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Egypt does not permit check-the-box elections. However, specific hybrid mismatch rules apply under the Egyptian Income Tax Law for cross-border transactions.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EGP 1,000,000 (one million Egyptian Pounds) in annual taxable supplies
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory real-time electronic invoicing through the Egyptian Tax Authority's E-Faktura platform; all invoices require digital stamping and clearance before issuance to customers.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Eligibility for 0% VAT rate on exported goods and certain services provided they are exported and foreign currency proceeds are repatriated to Egypt.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Tax authorities may audit and claw back zero-rated VAT if documentation is insufficient; penalties include fines up to 100% of evaded tax, interest, and potential criminal prosecution for fraudulent claims.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Egypt operates a managed floating exchange-rate regime under the Central Bank of Egypt (CBE). Current-account transactions (trade in goods/services, interest, dividends, branch remittances) are de facto convertible through authorised banks, subject to submission of underlying documentation such as contracts, invoices, customs forms, and tax withholding certificates. Profit remittances require an audit-ready chain from the Egyptian LLC's audited financial statements, the CBE foreign-exchange request form, and proof of tax settlement; false declarations invite CBE sanctions and suspension of FX facilities. Capital-account transfers (foreign direct investment equity injection, liquidation surplus, or capital reduction proceeds) require formal registration of the investment with the General Authority for Investment (GAFI) and must be executed through a licensed bank; the principal is transferable only after the bank verifies the original inward remittance trail. Since the 2016 FX liberalisation, no isolated prior CBE approval is needed for routine trade payments, but commercial banks apply their own KYC/AML controls and may defer payment where the instructing company has no visible operational footprint. The Egyptian pound is still a restricted local currency; it cannot be freely exported or traded outside Egypt, and all onshore settlements must occur in EGP or in foreign-currency accounts held with an Egyptian authorised bank.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under CBE Regulation No. 300/2020 as updated and Articles 110-120 of the Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194/2020, export proceeds for manufactured goods, including designer blind-box toys, must be collected through an Egyptian licensed bank and repatriated to the exporter's foreign-currency account within 90 calendar days from the date of shipment (bill of lading/airway bill date). There is no mandatory fixed conversion ratio into Egyptian pounds; exporters may retain up to 100% of export proceeds in a foreign-currency account and convert only as needed for domestic tax payments, salaries, or local supplier invoices. To prove compliance, the exporter must present the customs export declaration (ACD), commercial invoice, packing list, transport documents, and the underlying sales contract to the negotiating bank. Failure to meet the repatriation deadline exposes the exporter to CBE Foreign Exchange Violations Committee penalties, including fines up to 100% of the uncollected amount, suspension of the corporate FREE (Foreign Exchange) card, and potential cancellation of the exporter's no-objection certificate for future FX operations.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Low. Legal constraints: Under the Central Bank and Banking System Law No. 194/2020 and the Egyptian Payment Systems Law No. 18/2019, only entities licensed by the CBE as banks, specialised payment service providers, or e-money institutions may lawfully hold client funds and execute payments for onshore corporate accounts. An offshore digital EMI (non-resident fintech wallet or neobank) is not recognised as a bank for the Egyptian statutory framework and cannot operate as the primary treasury account for EG_LLC. Using such an EMI for trade settlement, payroll, or operational receivables would constitute unauthorised cross-border payment processing, risk penalties before the CBE FX Violations Committee, and break the evidentiary chain needed for customs, VAT, and profit repatriation. Offshore EMIs have no direct connection to CBE infr, the Egyptian wire transfer system, or EFT/MTC clearing, and cannot issue valid documentation for Egyptian tax authorities. An offshore EMI may be used only as an auxiliary collection angle by a CBE-licensed payment aggregator for final settlement into an Egyptian bank, and only where the aggregate fund-flow is fully reported and reconciles with export declarations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory. CBE anti-money-laundering rules require the legal representative (general manager or chairman) and, in practice, at least one ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) to appear personally at the Egyptian bank branch for the original KYC interview. The interview must be conducted by the bank's compliance officer, recorded in the bank's compliance minutes, and the file must be signed by the customer. Remote-only account opening is not recognised as a standard regulatory path for Egyptian LLCs; digital submission may be used for pre-screening but a face-to-face session is mandatory before account activation. All authorised signatories must be identified with original IDs; non-Egyptian shareholders must provide passport copies, Egyptian residence permits or entry stamps, and documented evidence of the source of funds for the capital contribution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Ultimate beneficial owner or controlling shareholder appears on a sanctions list, FATF grey/black list, or CBE adverse AML matrix.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a certified local-counsel legal opinion and UBO source-of-wealth statement; passport and national ID copies; residence proof; a sworn affidavit detailing commercial rationale for the jurisdiction relationship; and the UBO register filed under the Egyptian Companies Law showing the full ownership chain and proportionate rights.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between declared business activity (designer toys manufacturing) and transaction profile: large aggregate inflows from worldwide e-commerce platforms with low unit prices but no corresponding customs declarations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide an auditable transaction dossier including Shopify Payments, Stripe, and local POS settlement reports, customer order logs, HS6-coded commercial invoices for each shipment, customs export declarations (ACD), air-waybill and courier proofs (DHL/FedEx), VAT e-invoices as filed with the Egyptian Tax Authority, and a reconciliations statement from the Egyptian customs broker.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undercapitalised Egyptian LLC: initial paid-in capital appears nominal relative to expected monthly turnover of the online designer toy business.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the notarised share subscription agreement, GAFI investment certificate, bank credit advice showing the actual capital transfer, asset valuation report if the contribution included tooling/molds, a 24-month cash-flow forecast, and the parent company's audited financial statements for the last three years demonstrating the capacity to capitalise the Egyptian entity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Same UBO controls multiple Egyptian entities and intercompany fund flows are frequent (potential disguised tax or FX avoidance).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide an intra-group services agreement evidencing arm`s-length remuneration, a transfer pricing file prepared under the Egyptian Transfer Pricing Guidelines, a group organisational chart with shared-cost allocation methodology, and full-board minutes explaining the commercial purpose of each intercompany cash flow.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound capital injection must be routed through an Egyptian authorised bank in Egyptian pounds or a permitted foreign currency using a SWIFT MT103 wire. The remitter must be the foreign parent / shareholder identified in the Egyptian Commercial Register; the beneficiary must be recorded as the exact legal name of EG_LLC. The remittance instruction field (Field 70) must state the purpose code per the CBE Balance of Payments classification for direct investment, using the words 'CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION' or 'DIRECT INVESTMENT EQUITY'. The receiving Egyptian bank will verify the Commercial Register extract, Articles of Association, share subscription resolution, GAFI investment certificate, and an AML source-of-funds declaration. Funds must be credited to a Capital Escrow Account and cannot be released for operating purposes until the capital increase is duly registered with the Commercial Registry and the Egyptian Tax Authority's tax card is amended. The bank compliance officer will issue an inward transfer verification receipt which must be preserved as the definitive evidence for future capital repatriation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Trade settlements for imported resin, PVC, paints, packaging, and injection tooling may be executed by: (1) direct SWIFT MT103 telegraphic transfer for open-account trade under a bank-approved threshold; or (2) an irrevocable commercial letter of credit (L/C) at sight or usance for high-value or new-supplier transactions. The Egyptian bank will assign the applicable CBE trade purpose code and require the commercial invoice, Bill of Lading / Airway Bill, packing list, and the Egyptian customs import declaration (IDU) to effect settlement. For TT payments, the bank may request a supplier contract and prior import customs registration; for L/C transactions, the bank issues an MT700 and will check presentation documents under UCP 600. All outbound FX payments must be covered by a valid underlying transaction and cannot be made ahead of the contractual due date without the bank's treasury pre-approval. The company must route all import settlement exclusively through its Egyptian licensed bank to maintain the full record chain for VAT input credit, customs reconciliation, and tax audits.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable outright FX forward contracts with an Egyptian licensed bank, tenor up to 180 days, supported by documentary evidence of a genuine underlying trade import/export exposure; speculative forward-only hedging is not permitted.

Cross-currency swaps (CCS) between EGP and USD/EUR entered into with an Egyptian authorised bank for balance-sheet liability hedging, provided the swap proceeds are directly applied to a documented foreign-currency loan or other financial liability and that internal hedge policy has been board-approved.

Non-deliverable forward contracts (NDFs) may be used only where the Central Bank of Egypt has expressly authorised the structure or where the NDF is executed as an offshore hedge through a licensed Egyptian bank's treasury desk and is bracketed to a genuine commercial flow; pure offshore speculative NDF contracts are not lawful for onshore Egyptian corporates.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax Return (Form No. 35) and Audited Financial Statements
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months from fiscal year end; April 30 following December 31 year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty: EGP 1,000 fixed plus EGP 500 per month of delay; non-filing may trigger assessment and license suspension

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Value-Added Tax Return and Reconciliation
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual reconciliation filing by January 31 for prior calendar year; monthly returns due by end of following month
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing: EGP 20 daily per return up to EGP 2,000; late payment interest at 2.5% monthly on VAT due

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial Registration Renewal and Annual Registry Fee Payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: General Authority for Investment and Free Zones (GAFI) - Commercial Registry
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Renewal due every 5 years on anniversary of initial registration; annual maintenance fee payable on the company's incorporation anniversary
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal fee up to EGP 2,000; prolonged non-renewal leads to administrative strike-off of trade licence

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Register Confirmation and Update
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation by March 31 each year; updates of ownership changes within 30 days of any share transfer
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain or confirm UBO records: warning, then fine up to EGP 100,000; repeated breach may lead to strike-off

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All Egyptian LLCs are legally required to appoint a certified independent auditor and file audited financial statements; no small-company exemption is available under the Companies Law
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Egyptian Accounting Standards (EAS), which are substantially aligned with IFRS

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The company must keep an updated register of ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) and annually confirm the register's accuracy to GAFI by March 31. Any share transfer during the year must be recorded in the statutory registers and filed with the Commercial Registry within 30 days; the UBO register is updated and re-confirmed with each change
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Company Contracts and Conflict-of-Interest Disclosures

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 22.5% on net taxable income under Law No. 195 of 2020 (Egypt's unified Income Tax Law, effective for tax years commencing on or after 1 January 2021)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: SME presumptive regime for annual gross revenue not exceeding EGP 20,000,000: 0.5% of revenue up to EGP 2,000,000; 1% of revenue between EGP 2,000,001 and EGP 10,000,000; 2.5% of revenue between EGP 10,000,001 and EGP 20,000,000. Investment Law No. 72 of 2017 grants a 5-year income tax holiday, extendable to 7 years, for projects located in Zone A governorates and the Suez Canal Economic Zone, subject to minimum employment and capital conditions. Export-oriented manufacturing may benefit from accelerated depreciation and customs-drawback-related cost deductibility.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Egyptian Tax Form No. 26 (Corporate Income Tax Return for capital companies), filed digitally through the Egyptian Tax Authority (ETA) e-filing portal at www.incometax.gov.eg, with integrated e-invoice and e-receipt cross-checks.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return; quarterly advance (provisional) tax payments are collected on account based on the prior year's assessed tax, with final settlement in the annual return.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: No later than four months after the close of the fiscal year. For a calendar-year LLC, the return is due by 30 April. The assessed tax shown on the return is payable upon filing; no general extension is available absent ETA discretionary relief.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 – Taxpayer Identification and Fiscal Year
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, commercial registry number, tax card number, fiscal-year period, registered address, and sector code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The Egyptian LLC files this in its own name as a resident legal person; the non-resident parent is not a co-signatory, but its name, jurisdiction, and shareholding percentage must be disclosed in the related-party shareholder schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 – Principal Activity and Product Code
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Description of the main commercial activity and the applicable ISIC/HS code.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter 'Manufacture of games and toys – rotocasting, injection molding, and airbrush finishing of vinyl designer collectibles (ISIC 3240 / NAICS 339930)'. If the foreign parent is deemed to have a permanent establishment through local activity, do not merge the parent's income on this form.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross sales from designer blind-box toys, direct e-commerce sales (Shopify, Stripe), POS sales, wholesale distribution, licensing income, and export proceeds.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Worldwide revenue of the Egyptian LLC must be declared. Cross-border e-commerce sales into GCC/MENA markets are taxable on the LLC's worldwide income; the foreign parent's sales commission structure must accord with transfer pricing and not be treated as undisclosed revenue.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Raw materials (PVC, resin, packaging), direct labor, factory overhead, subcontract rotocasting and injection costs, airbrushing consumables, and inventory adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Intercompany purchases from the foreign parent or affiliated molding shops in China/UAE must be priced at arm's length; the local file must support the cost build-up; a 100% foreign-supplier pass-through without value addition invites TP re-characterization.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Marketing and brand-promotion spend, freight, logistics, platform transaction fees, professional fees, rent, utilities, and administrative overhead, with separate re-addition of non-deductible items.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Royalties, technical service fees, and interest paid to the non-resident parent are deductible only if 20% final withholding tax has been withheld and remitted to the ETA; absent proper invoice and WHT proof, payments are non-deductible.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 – Depreciation, Capital Allowances, and Loss Carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Schedules of fixed assets (molds, rotocasting machines, airbrushing booths, IT equipment), tax depreciation at ETA-prescribed straight-line rates, and application of prior-year tax losses subject to the 5-year limit.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Imported machinery from the related party must be valued at arm's length; transfer of used molds or tooling must be supported by third-party valuation or CUP data; temporary unused production capacity does not justify accelerated tax depreciation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 7 – Tax Base and Rate Computation
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net taxable income after all adjustments, application of the 22.5% headline rate or the SME presumptive revenue-based rate, and any investment or export incentives claimed.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the LLC claims the SME presumptive regime, aggregate related-party revenue cannot be fragmented to artificially remain below the EGP 20,000,000 threshold; consolidation rules attribute the parent group's revenue to the Egyptian entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 8 – Advance Payments, Withholdings, and Foreign Tax Credits
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Quarterly provisional payments already made, domestic WHT suffered (e.g., interest or dividend income), and any foreign tax credits on cross-border income subject to Egyptian tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Dividend distributions to the parent are not deductible on this return and do not generate a credit; the 10% dividend WHT is a separate remittance made by the LLC as withholding agent against the parent's income.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an administrative fine in a range typically of EGP 10,000 to EGP 50,000 for corporate taxpayers, plus monthly delinquency interest of 2% per month (24% per annum) on unpaid tax. Persistent non-filing may result in suspension of the Tax Card, customs clearance denial, attachment of bank accounts, and criminal fines up to EGP 100,000; deliberate false declarations escalate to tax evasion prosecution.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on gross dividends distributed by the Egyptian LLC to all shareholders (resident or non-resident), withheld and remitted by the LLC at the time of distribution.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident beneficial owner must obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from its home tax authority, legalized or apostilled as applicable, covering the date of distribution. The shareholder then submits a Treaty Relief Application (ETA treaty form), a beneficial ownership declaration, corporate existence documents, and a LoB/PPT self-assessment to the Egyptian LLC before payment. The Egyptian LLC files the complete dossier with the ETA to obtain a reduced-rate directive for the dividend payment; if tax is over-withheld, the non-resident may apply to the ETA for refund within the statutory five-year claim window. The Egyptian LLC remains jointly liable for under-withheld tax if treaty documentation is defective or the beneficial ownership declaration is fraudulent.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding tax is 20% on gross royalties for trademarks, designs, know-how, and software; 20% on debt interest paid to non-residents; and 20% on technical and management service fees unless the recipient has a taxable permanent establishment in Egypt. Treaty reduction generally ranges from 10% to 15% for royalties and interest (e.g., 10% for royalties under the Egypt–UAE DTA and 10–15% under several EU and OECD counterpart treaties), subject to TRC, beneficial ownership, and principal-purpose-test compliance; loan notes from the parent must carry market-rate interest and be properly documented to avoid debt-equity re-characterization.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous Local File and Master File are mandatory when the aggregate annual value of related-party transactions exceeds EGP 10,000,000; CbC reporting applies to multinational groups with consolidated annual revenue of at least EGP 10,000,000,000. The Egyptian LLC must also complete the related-party disclosure table in Form No. 26; the ETA may assess penalties and adjust margins where documentation is not produced within 30 days of an audit request.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Egypt does not operate the Gulf-Cooperation-Council-style Economic Substance Regulations. Substance requirements are enforced through the general anti-avoidance rule (GAAR) in Law No. 195 of 2020, the BEPS Multilateral Instrument principal-purpose test (Egypt signed the MLI in 2019), and ETA's substance-over-form jurisprudence. A designer blind-box toy LLC with negligible local payroll, no physical manufacturing premises, no commercial decision-making, and no independent business rationale will be disregarded for treaty and incentive purposes; the foreign parent may be deemed to have a permanent establishment in Egypt, and the LLC may be reclassified as a shell conduit subject to full 22.5% tax, including back interest and penalties.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion via Under-Declaration and False Accounting
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Omitting cash or e-commerce revenues from the Form No. 26 return, fabricating supplier invoices for injected vinyl components, inflating manufacturing costs, or manipulating inventory counts to eliminate taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal prosecution under Law No. 195 of 2020 with imprisonment up to 5 years and a fine of no less than 3 times the evaded tax; mandatory addition of the evaded tax plus 2% monthly delinquency interest; the ETA may also impose the maximum EGP 50,000 to EGP 100,000 administrative fine and suspend the taxpayer's Tax Card, blocking import/export and contracting.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and statutory managers are personally pursued where the LLC is a mere façade; the court may pierce the corporate veil and attach personal bank accounts and real estate. Individual travel bans (no-fly orders) are commonly issued against responsible officers controlling the flow of unremitted funds.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Sham Substance for Treaty or Incentive Abuse
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Routing designtoy royalties, dividends, or group manufacturing contracts through the Egyptian LLC solely to access the 5-year Zone A/SCZone holiday or a reduced treaty rate, without local production, staff, premises, or real economic risk.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ETA application of GAAR to disregard the entity; cancellation of all tax holidays and treaty rate relief; reassessment at the 22.5% statutory rate with back-tax, 2% monthly delay interest, and a punitive fine up to 5 times the tax avoided; referral to the Egyptian Money Laundering Combating Unit if cross-border fund flows are structured to conceal beneficial ownership.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be disqualified, made subject to asset freezes, and criminally sanctioned for submitting false substance declarations to the General Authority for Investment (GAFI); in insolvency, liquidators can seek civil restitution against managers for the benefit obtained from the sham structure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Withholding Tax and Social Insurance Trust-Fund Misappropriation
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deducting 10% dividend WHT, 20% royalty or interest WHT, or payroll tax/social insurance premiums from amounts otherwise payable, but failing to remit the sums to the ETA or NOSI within the statutory deadlines.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The unremitted amounts are deemed misappropriated public funds; the ETA imposes 2% monthly late-payment interest, administrative fines of up to the amount withheld, and can initiate criminal confiscation procedures against the company's assets. The Tax Clearance Certificate is withheld until full settlement.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors are jointly and severally personally liable for withheld taxes as statutory trustees regardless of corporate dissolution or restructuring; civil restitution, travel bans, and personal bankruptcy risk apply if the withheld funds were diverted to group funding, shareholder loans, or personal expenses.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting large-volume cash payments for designer blind-box toys through local POS terminals and intentionally failing to record them in the e-invoice system to evade VAT and CIT, or splitting cash transactions into amounts below EGP 10,000 to avoid Egyptian AML identification thresholds and CBE currency-declaration rules.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Egypt's AML Law No. 80 of 2002 (as amended), sanctions include imprisonment of up to 7 years and fines of up to EGP 5 million or the value of the laundered funds, whichever is greater; the EMLCU can freeze company bank accounts, seize proceeds, and impose ancillary confiscation penalties on the LLC's entire commercial operation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers face parallel criminal indictment for failure to file Suspicious Activity Reports (SARs), travel bans pending investigation, personal confiscation of benefits, and disqualification from managing any commercial company; the corporate form does not shield individuals in AML prosecutions.
